source.title: The IntCal20 Northern Hemisphere Radiocarbon Age Calibration Curve (0–55 cal kBP)
source.evidence: Because of the large amount of new data under consideration, particularly from 0 to 3000 cal BP, a minimum length for datasets was adopted to allow a realistic assessment of their reliability against existing datasets (10 measurements for decadal samples, 15 for 5-ring samples, 20 for 3-ring samples or 100 for single-year data, if not replicated by a second laboratory).

source.title: The IntCal20 Northern Hemisphere Radiocarbon Age Calibration Curve (0–55 cal kBP)
source.evidence: The older portion of the IntCal20 curve also has a larger range in Δ14C, with higher values than the highest IntCal13 values and lower values than the lowest IntCal13 values.

source.title: Fixed and random effects models: making an informed choice
source.evidence: The only reason to choose FE is if (1) higher-level variables are of no interest whatsoever, (2) there are no random slopes in the true DGP, or (3) there are so few level-2 entities that random slopes are unlikely to be estimable.
